text: Two environmental screening processes under the Environmental Assessment Act were initiated this past Spring for independent proposals to operate existing backup diesel generators during periods of peak electricity demand. At 220 Simcoe Street, Bell Canada proposes to operate three of four generators to provide up to 3.755 megawatts of electricity. And at 120 Pearl Street, Enwave Energy Corporation proposes to operate one generator to provide up to 2.250 megawatts of electricity. These proposals are a concern for air quality in the vicinity of each site, and may also have implications for a wider area. During periods of peak electricity demand, the weather is often extremely hot and humid, and air quality can already be a challenge for vulnerable individuals. City Council on July 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 30, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council request the Medical Officer of Health to assess the health impact of the proposed use of diesel generators for energy production during peak energy demand at 120 Pearl Street and 220 Simcoe Street, and to provide the findings to the Ministry of the Environment and Climate Change, the project proponent, and the Ward Councillor.
